title: root-cause-flow-explorer-spec
content:
Purpose / brief
This doc captures a proposed UX for a Root Cause Flow Explorer (RCFE) — a console panel intended for quick triage of request failure funnels (timeouts, 5xx, model errors and malformed outputs) and to suggest likely remediation actions. Target users: on-call SREs, infra/product engineers, and solutions engineers responding to customer incidents.

High-level goals
- Surface aggregated failure funnels so teams can understand where requests are dropping (network, router, runtime, model).
- Prioritize noisy / high-cost failure patterns and make it easy to jump from aggregate to sample-level replay.
- Offer lightweight automated suggestions (e.g., fallbacks to smaller context, increase timeouts, route to replica-pool) while keeping operators in control.
- Fit into Console -> Observability -> Incidents flow; must link to traces, logs, and request replay.

User journeys (examples)
1) Pager fires; SRE opens RCFE for the affected service + time window. Uses timeline to confirm spike in 5xx. Uses Sankey funnel to see 60% of failures originate after runtime and before model load (suggests model cold start). Drills into sample requests, hits request-replay with pinned model variant and reproduces failure.
2) Product engineer notices high cost from many retries. Filters RCFE by "retries > 2" and "embedding route" to find a degraded model variant. Uses the "compare variants" view to switch routing policy.
3) Support engineer investigating customer report: filters by customer-id tag, sees high latency bucket concentrated in us-west-2 region; uses trace links to open full trace in APM.

Primary UI panels (wireframe descriptions)
- Header bar
  - Date/time selector (preset windows + custom range), auto-suggested range from alert timestamps.
  - Primary filter row: service/route, model family, model variant, region, customer-id, API key.
  - Quick actions: export CSV, open trace, open alert, escalate.

- Top summary strip (left-to-right)
  - KPI chips: total requests, failure rate (p0), p90 latency, cost per 1k tokens, retry rate.
  - Small sparkline under each chip for the selected window.

- Main visualization area (three-column responsive layout)
  Column A: Funnel / Sankey (large)
    - Steps: ingress (api gateway) -> router -> auth/quotas -> serving runtime -> model (variant) -> post-processing.
    - Each step shows throughput and failure counts. Color-coded by error class (timeouts amber, 5xx red, model-error purple, malformed blue).
    - Hover reveals top failure signatures and top example request IDs (clickable).
    - Ability to collapse intermediate steps (e.g., hide auth) to focus.

  Column B: Heatmap + timeline
    - Error heatmap by minute for selected step(s).
    - Stacked timeline showing contribution by error type.
    - Anomaly markers where error rate deviates from baseline (auto-detected by ML scoring).

  Column C: Probable root-cause panel / suggestions
    - Top 3 hypotheses (confidence score): e.g., "Model cold-starts on variant v2 causing 45% of latency errors"; "KV cache miss storm for customer X".
    - Quick remediation actions (one-click) where safe: increase timeout for route, route subset to stable variant, enable local retry/backoff.
    - Buttons: open samples, create incident, assign to team, open perf profile.

- Bottom: request samples table + replay playground
  - Table shows sampled requests that match current filters. Columns: request_id, timestamp, latency, error_type, model_variant, region, token_count, linked_trace_id.
  - Inline actions: open raw request, open trace, replay (opens sandboxed replay runner with same headers + toggle model_variant/timeouts). Replay logs stored as a transient artifact for audit.

Data / telemetry requirements (assumptions)
- Aggregation keys: route_id, model_family, model_variant, region, customer_id, api_key.
- Required telemetry: request start/end, step markers (ingress, router-hand-off, runtime-queue, runtime-start, runtime-end, model-load, postprocess), error codes, token counts, selected tokenized prompt size, sampling fingerprint for request replay.
- Minimum sampling rate: 1% default but auto-increase to 100% for incident windows (configurable by SLO rule).
- Need correlation ids that persist through routing to runtime and model serving (critical).

Interaction details / edge cases
- Filtering should be additive with OR/AND toggles for advanced queries.
- Timeouts: if step-level durations are missing for some requests, flag them as "partial-trace" and surface in the funnel with dashed lines.
- When replaying, if the original model variant is unavailable, show an inline compatible-variants picker with notes on likely behavior differences (quantization, context window).
- Guardrails: one-click remediation actions that change routing or timeouts must require a confirmation modal with estimated impact and rollback link.

Accessibility & small screen behavior
- Sankey collapses to a vertical stacked bar on narrow screens.
- Keyboard-first navigation for requesting sample details and replay run.
- Color palette uses hatching and icons as well as color to encode error classes for color-blind users.

MVP scope (what to build first)
- RINF-4321: Error aggregation API (route + variant + region) + backend for funnel counts. Acceptance: endpoints return time-bucketed counts and top N signatures per step.
- RINF-4322: Sankey/funnel component and heatmap visualization (frontend). Acceptance: selectable steps, hover samples, responsive layout.
- RINF-4323: Request samples table + basic replay runner (sandboxed, non-destructive). Acceptance: replay uses stored request payload and returns reproducible result or deterministic error.
- RINF-4324: Probable root cause service prototype (rules + anomaly scoring). Acceptance: populate 3 hypotheses per incident with confidence score.

Backlog & grooming notes (prioritized)
- P1: Improve sampling escalation: autopromote sample rate to 100% for any alert that hits failure threshold for 3 consecutive 1-min buckets.
- P1: Persist replay logs to customer-accessible audit bucket with TTL 7d; ensure PII redaction.
- P2: Add model-variant diff view: tokenization differences and quantization flag.
- P2: Enable CSV export and shareable filtered links for incidents.
- P3: Add correlation with infra-level metrics (GPU memory pressure, host CPU) to surface non-model causes.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics
- Time to actionable triage: median under 8 minutes from alert to identified root-cause hypothesis (tracked via telemetry).
- Reduction in escalations to infra-team for model-caused incidents by 30% in quarter after release.
- Replay reproducibility: 95% reproducible behaviors for stored samples (excluding non-deterministic models).

Design questions to resolve in grooming
- What thresholds define the step boundaries? (e.g., router -> runtime vs runtime queue) Need engineering input on available trace markers.
- How will we surface model-specific semantic errors (e.g., hallucinations) vs transport errors? Requires mapping from model eval signals.
- UX for multi-tenant customers: how do we avoid leaking other customers' failure signatures when filtering by broad time windows? (Consider automatic tenant scoping).

Next steps (short term)
- Product to align with Applied ML and Serving Runtime on required trace markers (owner: Jordan Park) by EOD 2024-10-10.
- Schedule a 60m grooming session to convert MVP items into sprint tickets (owner: Elena Martinez).
- Engineering to spike on a lightweight Sankey proof-of-concept using existing aggregated API (owner: Samir Gupta, due 2024-10-17).

Appendix: quick mockup notes (visual shorthand)
- Header: left-aligned breadcrumbs, center filters, right actions.
- Funnel: widest step at top (ingress) narrowing down; each link annotated with failure count + % drop.
- Heatmap: rows = error type, columns = minute buckets; color intensity = count.
- Probable root cause: card UI with 3 stacked cards, each with confidence bar, sample links, and suggested actions.

Notes / open items
- Need privacy review for storing raw prompts in replay logs.
- Confirm service-level cost estimates for enabling 100% sampling during incidents.
- Explore embedding lightweight ML model to prioritize samples for developer review (future).

If this looks directionally correct, I'll schedule the grooming session and produce quick rectangular wireframes to pair with this doc. Comments inline welcome.
